slides.0.content: Fine Dining Design + Asian Cuisine Pairing + Level 4 Assessment — This final Level 4 lesson covers all 58 Loire Valley AOCs, synthesizing Loire's full range of styles into practical food-pairing applications for both European fine dining and Asian cuisine contexts.
slides.1.title: Fine Dining Design + Asian Cuisine Pairing + Level 4 Assessment
slides.1.content:
This course systematically reviews all 58 Loire Valley AOC terroir characteristics, with a focus on practical wine-pairing applications. Key pairing principles: Muscadet × shellfish (classic); Savennières × aged goat cheese; Vouvray Moelleux × foie gras; Sancerre × sashimi / Cantonese steamed fish; Chinon × Peking duck; Crémant-de-Loire × dim sum.

Through systematic study, you will be able to identify the typical styles of these AOCs and accurately describe their characteristics in both tasting and service contexts.
slides.2.title: Level 4 Final Assessment
slides.2.questions.0.question: Which best describes the scope of Loire Level 4?
slides.2.questions.0.options.0: All 58 Loire Valley AOCs — integrating geography, terroir, vintages, aging, and food pairing
slides.2.questions.0.explanation: Loire Level 4 is the advanced capstone module, covering all ~58 Loire Valley AOCs across four sub-regions (Pays Nantais, Anjou-Saumur, Touraine, Centre-Loire), plus satellite regions such as Côtes-d'Auvergne. The module integrates geographic visualization, climate analysis, vertical tasting, blind tasting soil diagnosis, and fine dining pairing into a comprehensive advanced certification framework.
